outcome: Renal functions (serum urea, creatinine, urine output, creatinine clearance, urinary creatinine, urinary pH, urinary sodium, fractional excretion of sodium, renal failure index, osmolality, urine potassium, urine specific gravity)
cohort: The study included 150 full-term perinatally asphyxiated neonates admitted to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).
finding: Renal dysfunction correlates well with increasing severity of asphyxia in terms of HIE staging, showing increased blood urea, serum creatinine, urinary sodium, FeNa, RFI, and a fall in creatinine clearance as HIE progressed.
mod_finding: Assisted vaginal delivery and emergency caesarean section were more common among cases of perinatal asphyxia compared to controls.
